questions.question: A financial services company is designing an IPsec site-to-site VPN between two data centers. The security team requires Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) so that a future compromise of the pre-shared key cannot decrypt previously captured traffic. Which IKEv2 configuration element enforces PFS on every rekey?
options: Lifetime reduction on the IKEv2 SA to 3600 seconds so that long-term key material is rotated frequently across both peers
A stronger encryption algorithm such as AES-256-GCM in the IKEv2 proposal applied to the data SA
Enabling dead peer detection (DPD) on both peers with a short interval and aggressive retry timer
A Diffie-Hellman group specified in the IPsec (Phase 2) proposal so that each child SA rekey performs a fresh DH exchange
questions.explanation: PFS is achieved by performing a fresh Diffie-Hellman exchange during each IPsec SA rekey. Configuring a DH group in the IPsec (Phase 2) proposal forces that new exchange, so even if long-term keys are later compromised, previously recorded sessions cannot be decrypted. Option A only shortens the SA lifetime — the same derived key material is reused without a new DH. Option B picks a stronger cipher, but the encryption algorithm has no bearing on whether a new DH happens at rekey. Option C is a liveness check that detects dead peers; it does not influence key derivation.

questions.question: An engineer is hardening the control plane of a core Cisco IOS-XE router. Traffic destined to the router itself (routing protocol updates, SSH, SNMP) must be rate-limited and classified so that a flood of ICMP does not exhaust CPU. Which feature should be configured?
options: Unicast Reverse Path Forwarding (uRPF) in strict mode applied on all WAN-facing ingress interfaces across both peers in the failover pair for symmetric behavior
Hardware-based ACL on each ingress interface denying all ICMP and limited SSH source ranges
Control Plane Policing (CoPP) with a service-policy applied to the control-plane interface that classifies and rate-limits punted traffic
Storm Control on uplink interfaces with an ICMP broadcast threshold and an action of err-disable
questions.explanation: CoPP classifies traffic punted to the route processor into policy classes (routing, management, monitoring, undesirable) and applies rate-limiters so that floods of any single class cannot starve legitimate control-plane traffic. Option A addresses spoofed source addresses, not control-plane protection. Option B drops traffic at the interface but cannot rate-limit per-class and ICMP is far from the only control-plane risk. Option D is a Layer 2 broadcast/multicast/unicast suppression feature on data-plane interfaces; it has no effect on traffic punted to the CPU.

questions.question: A security architect wants to prevent rogue DHCP servers on an access switch and also stop ARP spoofing between hosts in the same VLAN. Which combination of features must be enabled?
options: DHCP snooping with trusted uplinks plus Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) referencing the snooping binding table
Port-security sticky-MAC learning combined with DHCP option 82 insertion on the access ports
IP Source Guard on access ports plus static ARP entries for all default gateways and servers
BPDU Guard on all access ports together with Root Guard on the uplinks to the distribution layer with default platform tunables left unchanged for the deployment
questions.explanation: DHCP snooping builds a binding table of legitimate IP-to-MAC-to-port mappings and blocks DHCP server responses on untrusted ports, stopping rogue DHCP servers. Dynamic ARP Inspection then validates every ARP packet against that binding table, dropping gratuitous ARP spoofs. Option B controls how many MACs a port learns and tags DHCP requests but does neither rogue-server filtering nor ARP validation. Option C filters IP source addresses on the data plane and uses static ARP entries — useful supplements, but they do not validate dynamic ARP traffic between hosts. Option D protects spanning tree from BPDU injection and unauthorized root bridges; it does not touch DHCP or ARP.

questions.question: An enterprise is deploying Cisco ISE 3.x in a distributed architecture with two Policy Administration Nodes (PAN), two Monitoring nodes (MnT), and six Policy Service Nodes (PSN) across two data centers. Which statement about the PAN role is correct?
options: Both PAN nodes are active simultaneously and replicate configuration changes bi-directionally between the data centers
PANs provide RADIUS authentication services directly to network devices in addition to holding the configuration database for the documented enterprise reference architecture diagrams
Any PSN can be promoted to PAN automatically if both PANs fail, using a Raft-style election among healthy nodes
Only the primary PAN accepts configuration changes; the secondary PAN is a warm standby promoted manually or via auto-failover
questions.explanation: In ISE, only the primary PAN is writeable. The secondary PAN receives replicated configuration and becomes writeable only after a failover (manual, or auto-failover if configured). Option A is wrong because PAN replication is one-way primary-to-secondary, not bi-directional active/active. Option B is wrong because RADIUS authentication is handled by PSNs, not by PANs. Option C is wrong because ISE does not auto-promote PSNs to PAN; the operator either fails over to the secondary PAN or rebuilds.

questions.question: A network engineer is configuring 802.1X on Cisco Catalyst switches. Corporate laptops authenticate with EAP-TLS using machine certificates, while IP phones and printers lack 802.1X supplicants. The switch port must try 802.1X first and then fall back to MAB if no EAPOL response is received. Which command accomplishes this ordering?
options: dot1x host-mode multi-auth on the access port to allow multiple methods to coexist on the same port
dot1x pae authenticator together with mab enabled on the port, leaving method order to default behaviour
authentication event no-response action authorize vlan 99 so unanswered EAPOL drops into a guest VLAN
authentication order dot1x mab followed by authentication priority dot1x mab on the access port
questions.explanation: The `authentication order` command controls which method is tried first; `authentication priority` controls which method can preempt an existing session. Setting both to dot1x-then-mab guarantees 802.1X is attempted first and MAB is used only if the endpoint does not respond to EAPOL. Option A only changes how many hosts the port allows; it does not order methods. Option B enables both methods but relies on default ordering, which may not be deterministic on every platform/version. Option C handles the EAP no-response event by assigning a guest VLAN, which is a different fallback path that bypasses MAB.

questions.question: A company wants to enforce user-based segmentation without rewriting ACLs on every switch. Users are tagged at ingress based on their ISE authorization policy, and enforcement decisions are made at egress switches using those tags. Which technology provides this model?
options: Cisco TrustSec with Security Group Tags (SGT) assigned at ingress and SGACLs evaluated at egress
Private VLANs combined with port-based ACLs on each access switch to isolate user groups
MACsec with downlink encryption between access switches and per-VLAN ACLs at distribution using the recommended Cisco Validated Design template values
VRF-Lite with per-user route-leaking policies maintained at every Layer 3 hop
questions.explanation: TrustSec assigns an SGT to each authenticated session at ingress via ISE authorization. The tag is propagated inline or via SXP, and egress devices apply SGACLs (source-SGT to destination-SGT matrices). This decouples policy from IP addresses and VLANs. Option B isolates ports within a VLAN but offers no user-aware policy and still requires per-switch ACL maintenance. Option C provides Layer 2 encryption between devices; it does not carry identity for policy decisions. Option D scales poorly and is operationally infeasible at per-user granularity.

questions.question: An engineer observes that a Cisco Secure Firewall (FTD) managed by FMC is blocking legitimate HTTPS traffic to a business partner site because SSL decryption cannot inspect it. The partner uses certificate pinning. What is the correct action?
options: Import the partner's private key into FMC and use Decrypt-Known-Key for the destination
Create a Do Not Decrypt rule matching the partner domain (SNI or URL category) in the SSL policy
Switch the global decryption policy from Decrypt-Resign to Decrypt-Known-Key so pinned apps pass as documented in the deployment guide
Disable the SSL policy entirely on the access control rule that matches partner traffic
questions.explanation: Pinned applications reject any certificate not matching the exact pinned copy, so Decrypt-Resign always breaks them. The supported approach is to add a Do Not Decrypt rule for the specific destination (URL category, SNI, or application) while keeping decryption enabled globally. Option A is not possible — you do not own the partner's private key. Option C still attempts decryption, just with a known key, which you also do not possess. Option D removes decryption far too broadly and leaves legitimate inbound inspection disabled.

questions.question: A security team is rolling out Cisco Umbrella as the primary DNS-layer security control. The CISO requires that users on managed corporate laptops receive granular, user-level policies even when off the corporate network. Which deployment method meets this requirement?
options: Deploy Umbrella Virtual Appliances (VAs) in each branch to forward DNS to the Umbrella resolvers
Point internal DNS forwarders to the Umbrella resolvers using conditional forwarding from the corporate AD DNS
Configure DHCP to push Umbrella resolvers 208.67.222.222 and 208.67.220.220 to clients on every site
Install the Cisco Umbrella Roaming Client (or the AnyConnect Umbrella module) on each managed endpoint
questions.explanation: DHCP-based and VA-based deployments only apply while users are on the corporate network and identify clients at the network level rather than per user. The Umbrella Roaming Client (standalone or as an AnyConnect/Secure Client module) follows the device everywhere, encrypts DNS to Umbrella, and supports granular user/identity-based policies off-network. Option A relies on the user being in the branch. Option B works only for clients pointed at the internal forwarder. Option C is anonymous (resolver-only) and identifies by source IP, not user.

questions.question: A developer integrates a third-party application with Cisco FMC using the REST API. The application retrieves access control rules every 30 seconds. After a week, the requests start failing with HTTP 429. What is the most likely cause?
options: The API token has expired and FMC is returning a generic 429 instead of the documented 401
The client is missing the Content-Type: application/json header on its GET requests
FMC is rate-limiting the client because the polling frequency exceeds the documented per-client cap
The FMC REST API requires explicit re-authentication every 1000 calls regardless of token lifetime consistent with the published platform best-practice guide
questions.explanation: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests indicates rate limiting. FMC caps REST API calls (typically 120 messages per minute per client/IP). Reducing polling frequency, using subscription-based mechanisms, or spacing calls fixes the issue. Option A is wrong because an expired token returns 401 Unauthorized, not 429. Option B is wrong because a missing/invalid content type returns 415 Unsupported Media Type. Option D invents a behavior — FMC does not enforce a fixed-call re-auth cycle; token lifetime governs re-auth.

questions.question: A manufacturing company uses Cisco Stealthwatch (Secure Network Analytics) to detect anomalous behavior. Analysts want to identify lateral movement where an internal host suddenly starts communicating with many internal hosts on uncommon ports. Which Stealthwatch feature best detects this?
options: Custom Security Events matching specific SGT-to-SGT flows defined by the analyst
Behavioral algorithms feeding the Concern Index, with built-in detections for internal recon and scanning
Encrypted Traffic Analytics (ETA) for TLS visibility against malware-in-encryption signatures evaluated against the customer's compliance and audit baseline
Host Lock violations configured per host group to alert on policy-disallowed conversations
questions.explanation: Stealthwatch baselines normal east-west traffic patterns per host and raises the Concern Index when behavior deviates significantly, such as scanning many internal peers on uncommon ports. Option A requires the analyst to know the SGT pairs in advance and matches static patterns; it does not detect anomalies. Option C focuses on malware-in-encryption metadata, not lateral movement patterns. Option D is a static policy violation mechanism: useful where rules are pre-declared, but it does not detect behavioural anomalies.

questions.question: An engineer must enforce posture compliance so that only laptops with up-to-date Windows patches and a running AV agent can access corporate resources. Non-compliant devices receive remediation resources. Which Cisco ISE feature provides this?
options: Cisco ISE Posture Assessment using the AnyConnect/Secure Client Posture module with remediation actions
Cisco ISE Guest Services with sponsored access and a self-registration portal for visitors
Cisco ISE Profiling with DHCP and SNMP probes that classify each connecting endpoint by type aligned with the SOC operating procedures and runbook entries
Cisco ISE TACACS+ command authorization for privileged device administration sessions
questions.explanation: The ISE Posture Module (inside AnyConnect/Secure Client) evaluates the endpoint against posture policies (patch level, AV, registry, processes). Non-compliant devices receive a restricted dACL and a URL redirect to a remediation portal (patch server, AV update). Option B is for visitor authentication, not endpoint compliance. Option C identifies device type but does not evaluate compliance posture. Option D is for device administration AAA, not endpoint posture.

questions.question: A company's Cisco Secure Email (ESA) is receiving a spike in spoofed messages claiming to be from the CEO. The domain has SPF published but many messages still reach the inbox. What additional email authentication mechanism should be deployed and enforced?
options: Enable Sender IP Reputation (SBRS) to block senders below the configured reputation floor documented in the change-management ticket prior to rollout
Enable Graymail detection and Safe Unsubscribe to filter promotional and bulk mail
Use Forged Email Detection only, with a custom dictionary of executive display names
Configure DMARC with a reject policy in DNS, combined with DKIM signing, and enable DMARC verification on the ESA
questions.explanation: SPF alone only validates the envelope return-path; attackers can still spoof the From header. DMARC aligns SPF or DKIM with the From header and instructs receivers to reject non-aligned mail when `p=reject` is published. The ESA must also be configured to verify DMARC for inbound mail. Option A blocks low-reputation senders but does nothing for header spoofing from neutral or good-reputation IPs. Option B targets graymail (marketing/bulk), not spoofing. Option C is a useful supplement for impersonation by display name but cannot enforce authentication-based reject decisions on its own.

questions.question: A SOC analyst investigates a malware detection on an endpoint reported by Cisco Secure Endpoint. They need to see every file the process executed and every network connection it made, across time. Which Secure Endpoint feature provides this timeline?
options: Prevalence widget on the SecureX ribbon showing how common a hash is across the install base
Indications of Compromise (IoC) dashboard summarising recently triggered IoC rules
Retrospective Detection alerts that re-evaluate previously seen files after disposition changes as configured in the standard template provided by the vendor
Device Trajectory (combined with File Trajectory) showing chronological process, file, and network activity
questions.explanation: Device Trajectory shows a chronological process/file/network activity timeline for a specific host, while File Trajectory tracks where a specific SHA-256 was seen across the estate. Both together are essential for investigating scope and root cause. Option A is a quick prevalence lookup, not a timeline. Option B aggregates IoC counts but does not provide per-host activity history. Option C is a retroactive alerting mechanism, not an investigation timeline.

questions.question: An engineer configures a Cisco ASA running multiple context mode. Which statement is correct about the admin context?
options: Any user-created context can be designated as the admin context; it is used to reach system execution space and other contexts via `changeto context`
The admin context only stores licensing information and cannot pass production traffic of its own
The admin context must always be configured in transparent mode regardless of the other contexts' modes

The admin context is reserved for system-wide failover and file access only, and its configuration is stored exclusively in flash:/admin.cfg applying the platform-defaults shipped on a fresh installation
questions.explanation: In multi-context ASA, you designate one user-created context as the admin context. From it, administrators log in and use `changeto context` to manage other contexts. It can also pass traffic like any other context. Option B is wrong because the admin context can pass traffic normally. Option C is wrong because admin-context mode (routed/transparent) is independent and can match the operator's needs. Option D fabricates a fixed filename and an artificial restriction; admin context configuration is stored like any other context.

questions.question: A company uses a private Cisco PKI for issuing certificates to VPN users. Employees who leave must have their certificates invalidated immediately. Which PKI component provides near-real-time revocation validation without downloading large files?
options: Certificate Revocation List (CRL) downloaded daily and cached locally on the validating gateway
SCEP auto-enrollment combined with very short certificate lifetimes to bound exposure
Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) responder queried per certificate validation
Key Recovery Agent (KRA) holding copies of issued private keys for incident recovery
questions.explanation: OCSP lets a verifier query the current status of a single certificate in real time, avoiding the latency and size of downloading entire CRLs. Option A is the legacy approach: a daily CRL is too stale and increasingly large as a CA scales. Option B reduces exposure but cannot revoke a still-valid certificate immediately; you wait for it to expire. Option D is a key-escrow mechanism for recovering encrypted data, unrelated to revocation status.

questions.question: A security architect is choosing an IPsec IKEv2 proposal. The traffic is high-throughput east-west between two data centers and must use authenticated encryption to avoid separate HMAC processing. Which algorithm combination should be selected?
options: AES-256-CBC with HMAC-SHA-256 integrity and DH group 14 for the key exchange
AES-256-GCM (authenticated encryption) paired with DH group 20 (ECP-384) and PRF SHA-384
3DES with HMAC-SHA-1 and DH group 5 to maximise compatibility with legacy equipment across both peers in the failover pair for symmetric behavior
ChaCha20-Poly1305 with DH group 2 for software platforms lacking AES acceleration
questions.explanation: AES-GCM is authenticated encryption: confidentiality and integrity are produced in a single pass, which is faster at high throughput than CBC+HMAC. DH group 20 (ECP-384) matches the 256-bit cipher strength, and PRF SHA-384 pairs with it. Option A uses CBC + separate HMAC, which adds a second pass. Option C uses 3DES and SHA-1 — both deprecated — with weak DH group 5. Option D uses an algorithm that is not yet a standard IKEv2 suite on most Cisco platforms and pairs it with the badly outdated DH group 2.

questions.question: A DevSecOps team wants to catch vulnerable dependencies and insecure code patterns before the application is built and deployed. Which practice implements this shift-left principle?
options: Runtime application self-protection (RASP) agents installed in production to block exploits inline
Quarterly third-party penetration testing against the staging environment with manual report turnover with default platform tunables left unchanged for the deployment
Periodic Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST) scans against the production web application
SAST (Static Application Security Testing) and Software Composition Analysis (SCA) running on every pull request
questions.explanation: Shift-left means finding defects as early as possible. SAST analyzes source code for insecure patterns, and SCA inspects dependency manifests (package-lock, pom.xml) for known CVEs. Running both automatically on every PR blocks vulnerable code from being merged. Option A protects after deployment, which is the rightmost stage of the lifecycle. Option B is too infrequent and lags developer feedback by months. Option C runs after the app is built and deployed, which is a much later stage than shift-left.

questions.question: A Cisco Secure Web Appliance (WSA) is deployed in explicit proxy mode. Users report that after enabling HTTPS decryption, certain banking and payroll sites present a browser certificate error. What is the correct remediation?
options: Disable HTTPS decryption globally and rely on URL category controls for all destinations
Switch from explicit to transparent WCCP mode so that certificates are not rewritten at the proxy for the documented enterprise reference architecture diagrams
Regenerate the WSA's HTTPS proxy root CA every 24 hours and push the new cert via GPO
Install the WSA's HTTPS proxy CA in the browser trust store, and add a pass-through (Do Not Decrypt) rule for pinned/regulated destinations
questions.explanation: When the WSA decrypts TLS, it presents a certificate signed by its own CA. Browsers must trust that CA (pushed via GPO). For regulated/pinned sites (banking, payroll), a pass-through decryption policy avoids re-signing. Option A removes all visibility for an over-broad fix. Option B does not change certificate behavior — transparent mode still re-signs when decryption is enabled. Option C breaks every client constantly and is operationally absurd.

questions.question: An engineer deploys Cisco Umbrella SIG for a remote branch. They want web traffic to be inspected by the cloud firewall and forwarded securely from the branch router. Which tunnel type should be configured on the ISR?
options: L2TPv3 pseudowire to the nearest Umbrella PoP carrying transparent Layer 2 frames
GETVPN group-member tunnel keyed by the central Key Server before egress to Umbrella
DMVPN Phase 3 spoke tunnel toward a hub ASA, which then forwards to Umbrella over IPsec
IPsec IKEv2 tunnel from the ISR directly to the Umbrella SIG headend at the nearest PoP
questions.explanation: Umbrella SIG supports IPsec IKEv2 tunnels from network devices (ISR, Meraki, etc.) to its cloud headends. Traffic is then inspected by Cloud-Delivered Firewall and the secure web gateway. Option A is a Layer 2 pseudowire technology that Umbrella does not accept as a tunnel type. Option B is for site-to-site groups with shared keys over a transport network, not for cloud ingress. Option C adds an unnecessary hairpin through a hub and is not the documented ingress method.

questions.question: A Cisco ISE administrator wants non-compliant devices to be automatically quarantined and later released once remediated, without requiring manual session termination. Which RADIUS mechanism makes the switch terminate the session and re-authenticate the endpoint?
options: SNMP traps from ISE telling the switch to bounce the access port after a posture failure using the recommended Cisco Validated Design template values
RADIUS Change of Authorization (CoA) issued by ISE per RFC 5176 to disconnect or reauthenticate the session
802.1X `held` state expiration after the supplicant exceeds the configured backoff timer
TACACS+ command accounting events forwarded to the switch to drop the session inline
questions.explanation: RFC 5176 RADIUS CoA lets ISE push a reauthentication or session termination to the NAS in real time. ISE uses this to dynamically enforce policy changes, such as moving a posture-violating endpoint into a restricted VLAN/dACL and back when remediated. Option A is a non-standard, indirect mechanism and not how ISE quarantines. Option C describes an automatic backoff in the supplicant state machine; it does not push policy changes from the policy server. Option D is for command authorization in device admin AAA, not endpoint policy changes.

questions.question: A healthcare company stores PHI in an AWS S3 bucket. They must ensure data is encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys and that access is restricted to specific IAM roles. Which AWS configuration meets these requirements?
options: Enable SSE-S3 server-side encryption and allow public read with a permissive bucket policy
Enable SSE-KMS with a customer-managed KMS key and restrict access via an IAM role plus bucket policy referencing the role ARN
Rely on TLS 1.2 in transit, since S3 encrypts everything at rest by default with AWS-managed keys consistent with the published platform best-practice guide
Use client-side encryption with a static key stored in the application configuration file
questions.explanation: SSE-KMS with a customer-managed CMK gives the customer control over key policy, rotation, and audit via CloudTrail. Combining it with an IAM role and a bucket policy referencing the role ARN ensures only authorized identities can decrypt. Option A allows public read of PHI, which is a direct compliance violation. Option C confuses transport with at-rest control and uses an AWS-owned key with no customer control. Option D bakes a long-lived static secret into source/config, which is poor key management.

questions.question: An engineer enables NetFlow on a Cisco Catalyst switch to feed Stealthwatch. Which NetFlow version exports variable-length templates allowing Layer 2 fields, MAC addresses, and application identifiers?
options: NetFlow v5 with its fixed Layer 3 record format and IPv4-only field set
NetFlow v9 (and its IETF-standard successor IPFIX) using extensible templates
SNMP RMON2 aggregating Layer 3/4 traffic statistics on a polling interval evaluated against the customer's compliance and audit baseline
sFlow v5 sampling and exporting packet snippets over UDP
questions.explanation: NetFlow v5 has a fixed record format and only IPv4 Layer 3 fields. NetFlow v9 introduced templates, making it extensible; IPFIX is its IETF standard. Both support Layer 2 MAC, IPv6, NBAR2 application IDs, and custom fields, which Stealthwatch consumes. Option A is the legacy fixed format and cannot carry Layer 2 or application fields. Option C is a polled MIB-based statistics protocol, not a flow export protocol. Option D is a sampling protocol with its own format and is not NetFlow.

questions.question: A Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) generates an intrusion event for a Snort rule. The SOC wants to automatically query Cisco Threat Response/SecureX and see the reputation of the source IP, file hashes, and related incidents. Which integration enables this pivot?
options: Stealthwatch endpoint licensing to enrich flows with endpoint context for the source IP
DNAC Assurance threat telemetry forwarded into FMC for in-line reputation lookups
SecureX ribbon and Threat Response integration enabling one-click pivots on observables
Cisco Defense Orchestrator (CDO) inventory sync between FMC and the cloud manager
questions.explanation: SecureX Threat Response aggregates context from multiple Cisco modules (Secure Endpoint, Umbrella, FMC, Email, Talos) and lets analysts pivot on observables (IP, hash, URL) with one click. The ribbon is the browser widget that surfaces this across product consoles. Option A enriches Stealthwatch flows but does not provide cross-product observable pivots. Option B is a campus assurance product, not a threat intelligence pivot platform. Option D is a configuration manager for ASA/FTD and does not perform threat lookups.

questions.question: A security engineer is designing SXP (SGT Exchange Protocol) between ISE and an older Catalyst switch that does not support inline SGT tagging. Which statement about SXP is correct?
options: SXP carries IP-to-SGT bindings over TCP from speakers to listeners, allowing devices without inline tagging support to learn tags for enforcement
SXP is a multicast protocol that floods SGT bindings to every TrustSec-capable device in the cluster
SXP uses UDP 4500 and requires IPsec for confidentiality between the speaker and listener
SXP can only run between ISE and the Cisco ISR family, and is not supported on Catalyst switches at all aligned with the SOC operating procedures and runbook entries
questions.explanation: SXP is a TCP-based protocol (default port 64999) that propagates IP-to-SGT bindings from tagging-capable devices (or ISE) to devices that cannot propagate tags inline. Speakers send bindings; Listeners receive and program their enforcement tables. Option B is wrong because SXP is unicast peer-to-peer over TCP, not multicast flooding. Option C is wrong because SXP is TCP-based and does not require IPsec; integrity and confidentiality come from MD5 password protection or TLS where supported. Option D is wrong because Catalyst, Nexus, ASR, and ISE all support SXP.

questions.question: A CIO is evaluating Cisco Secure Workload (Tetration). Which primary security benefit does it provide beyond traditional perimeter firewalls?
options: Automatic WAN link optimization between data centers using application-aware path selection
Certificate lifecycle management for internal web servers across the application estate
Application dependency mapping and zero-trust micro-segmentation enforced at the workload
Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) scrubbing at the network edge before traffic enters the data center
questions.explanation: Secure Workload collects telemetry from agents on every workload, discovers application dependencies, then generates and enforces microsegmentation policies (allow-list) at the host level. It works identically on bare metal, VMs, containers, AWS, Azure, and GCP. Option A is a SD-WAN problem space, not a Secure Workload feature. Option B is a PKI lifecycle concern handled by separate tooling. Option D is a network/edge service handled by scrubbing providers or anti-DDoS appliances.

questions.question: An engineer troubleshoots an IKEv2 site-to-site VPN stuck in MM_WAIT_MSG2. Both peers have matching proposals, PSKs, and reachable IPs. Which is the most likely cause?
options: The ISAKMP authentication method is set to rsa-sig on one peer while the other uses pre-shared keys
The crypto ACLs on the two sides describe overlapping subnets and therefore fail proxy-ID negotiation
Outbound UDP 500 or UDP 4500 is being blocked by an intermediate firewall, or NAT is rewriting the source without NAT-T
Mismatched IKEv2 SA lifetime values between the two peers prevent the responder from completing message 2 documented in the change-management ticket prior to rollout
questions.explanation: MM_WAIT_MSG2 in the phase-1 state machine means the initiator is waiting for the first response from the peer. The overwhelming cause is Layer 3/4: UDP 500 (or 4500 with NAT-T) is dropped by a firewall, or NAT is rewriting the source without NAT-T enabled. Option A would cause an authentication-method mismatch failure that appears in a later state with a clear error. Option B is a proxy-ID/traffic-selector concern that surfaces during child SA negotiation, not in MM_WAIT_MSG2. Option D fails at SA establishment, not at message 2 wait.

questions.question: A company wants to allow contractors temporary wireless access via a self-registration portal that emails a one-time password. Which ISE feature implements this?
options: Posture portal with the AnyConnect posture module performing compliance checks at registration
BYOD portal with EAP-TLS certificate enrollment for managed personal devices
Guest Services with a self-registered guest portal that delivers credentials by email or SMS
MyDevices portal for end users to associate, lose, or reinstate their own devices
questions.explanation: The ISE Self-Registered Guest Portal lets visitors create an account, optionally approved by a sponsor, and delivers credentials via email/SMS. Option A is for compliance checking on managed endpoints, not visitor onboarding. Option B provisions client certificates for managed/BYOD devices, not contractor short-term access. Option D allows users to manage devices they already own; it is not a guest registration flow.

questions.question: A penetration tester gains access to a VLAN through a vulnerable kiosk and sends double-tagged 802.1Q frames hoping to reach a protected VLAN. Which mitigation specifically prevents this VLAN hopping attack?
options: Assign the trunk's native VLAN to the same VLAN used by neighboring access ports for simplicity as configured in the standard template provided by the vendor and consistent with the published vendor reference
Disable DTP, hardcode access ports with `switchport mode access`, assign a dedicated unused native VLAN, and tag the native VLAN with `vlan dot1q tag native`
Enable BPDU Guard on all access ports so any unexpected BPDU shuts the port down
Enable Root Guard on uplinks to keep the existing root bridge stable during the attack
questions.explanation: Double-tagging attacks succeed when the native VLAN on a trunk is used by normal access ports and when DTP allows unsolicited trunk negotiation. Hardcoding access ports, disabling DTP, using a dedicated unused native VLAN, and tagging it prevent the attack. Option A actively makes the attack easier. Options C and D address spanning-tree attacks, not 802.1Q double-tagging.

questions.question: A Cisco Umbrella Investigate analyst notices a domain with a high risk score, recent registration, and fast-flux DNS. Which characteristic is the strongest indicator that this domain is likely used for malware C2?
options: The domain presents a TLS certificate issued by Let's Encrypt rather than a commercial CA
Short TTL DNS records with rapidly rotating IP addresses across many ASNs (fast-flux)
The WHOIS record uses a privacy proxy that hides the registrant's real contact details
The domain serves all content over HTTPS using TLS 1.3 with modern ciphers
questions.explanation: Fast-flux DNS (very short TTL, IPs changing quickly across many ASNs) combined with a brand-new registration is a strong malware/botnet C2 signal. Options A, C, and D are all common on entirely benign sites — free CAs, privacy proxies, and modern TLS are widely adopted and on their own carry almost no malicious signal.

questions.question: An engineer configures Cisco AnyConnect (Secure Client) remote access VPN on an ASA. Which feature steers only corporate subnets through the tunnel while sending Internet-bound traffic directly?
options: Transparent firewall mode with a Bridge Virtual Interface (BVI) at the head end
Split tunneling using a `split-tunnel-policy tunnelspecified` ACL listing corporate subnets
Hair-pinning with `same-security-traffic permit intra-interface` on the ASA outside interface
Full-tunnel posture with U-turn NAT translating client subnets to the outside interface
questions.explanation: Split tunneling with an include ACL (`tunnelspecified`) pushes only the listed subnets down the VPN, while everything else uses the client's local Internet. Option A is a Layer 2 firewall mode unrelated to tunnel selection. Option C enables client-to-client traffic to leave and re-enter the same interface; it does not steer Internet traffic locally. Option D forces all traffic through the tunnel, the opposite of what was asked.

questions.question: A Cisco Secure Email Gateway is configured with Advanced Malware Protection (AMP). A user reports that a file delivered yesterday is now being flagged as malicious. Which AMP capability is responsible for detecting previously-delivered malicious files after disposition changes?
options: Graymail detection that re-classifies delivered marketing mail after end-user complaints
Retrospective Detection (retrospection) that re-evaluates dispositions when threat intelligence changes
File Reputation as evaluated at the moment of delivery using the original verdict from Talos applying the platform-defaults shipped on a fresh installation
Outbreak Filters with URL rewriting and time-of-click safeguards on embedded links
questions.explanation: AMP continuously re-evaluates file dispositions. If a file originally marked clean is later judged malicious (through sandboxing or Talos intel), Retrospective Detection fires alerts and allows administrators to identify previously delivered copies across mail and endpoints. Option A targets bulk/promotional mail, not malware. Option C is the original verdict at delivery time — by definition it cannot detect a later change. Option D protects against malicious URLs but does not re-classify already-delivered file attachments.

questions.question: An engineer configures OSPF authentication between two Cisco routers. The security team requires strong integrity and replay protection rather than plain MD5. Which option should be configured?
options: `neighbor a.b.c.d password cisco` on the OSPF process, mirroring BGP-style neighbor authentication
`ip ospf authentication null` to disable authentication while documenting the design intent
Authentication using a key chain with cryptographic algorithm HMAC-SHA-256 and overlapping lifetimes
`ip ospf message-digest-key 1 md5 cisco` combined with `ip ospf authentication message-digest` on the interface
questions.explanation: Modern IOS/IOS-XE supports HMAC-SHA cryptographic authentication for OSPF using key chains with rotation and lifetimes. Legacy MD5 is still available but weaker. Option A is BGP/EIGRP-style neighbor password syntax and is not how OSPF authentication is configured. Option B explicitly disables authentication, which contradicts the requirement. Option D selects MD5 — the very algorithm the team wants to move away from.

questions.question: A CASB product (Cisco Cloudlock) flags that several employees uploaded sensitive CRM records to an unsanctioned third-party SaaS. Which cloud security concept does Cloudlock address?
options: Kubernetes admission control that validates pod specs before they are persisted to etcd
Shadow IT discovery and SaaS data security via API connectors and inline policy enforcement
DNS-layer malware filtering on user devices regardless of network location
IaaS hardening of compute and storage via security groups and identity-based access controls
questions.explanation: CASBs inspect SaaS activity via API and inline modes: they discover Shadow IT, classify data (DLP), and apply policy against unsanctioned or risky sharing. Cloudlock integrates with Salesforce, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, etc. Option A is a Kubernetes platform feature unrelated to SaaS posture. Option C is what Umbrella does (DNS resolution and blocking), not a CASB. Option D is what cloud-native security groups and CSPM tools cover.

questions.question: A corporate policy states that privileged network device administrators must authenticate with MFA and have their commands audited. Which protocol provides command-by-command authorization and accounting?
options: Kerberos with PKINIT, providing certificate-based authentication for Windows domain accounts
TACACS+ with command authorization and accounting between the device and the AAA server
LDAP with TLS for directory-based account lookups against an enterprise identity store
RADIUS with Access-Challenge messages used for token-based MFA on the management plane
questions.explanation: TACACS+ separates authentication, authorization, and accounting and can authorize each individual command and log it. RADIUS authorizes the session as a whole, not per command. ISE supports TACACS+ with the Device Admin license to provide per-command MFA and audit. Option A is an authentication protocol; it does not perform per-command authorization on Cisco devices. Option C provides authentication and identity lookup but no command-level authorization. Option D handles MFA flows but lacks the per-command authorization model.

questions.question: An architect is choosing between Cisco DMVPN and GETVPN for a large multi-site MPLS backbone where all sites must freely reach each other and encryption must preserve original source/destination addresses for multicast routing. Which technology fits best?
options: Site-to-site IKEv1 mesh tunnels between every pair of sites, sized to the worst-case any-to-any traffic
GETVPN (Group Encrypted Transport VPN) with a Key Server distributing group keys via GDOI
FlexVPN hub-spoke with IKEv2 and dynamic spoke-to-spoke shortcut tunnels via NHRP
DMVPN Phase 2 with mGRE and NHRP redirects between spokes through the hub
questions.explanation: GETVPN uses group keys distributed by a Key Server via GDOI. Because it does not tunnel-encapsulate, the original IP header is preserved, which lets MPLS routing and multicast work natively across the encrypted overlay. Option A scales as O(n²) tunnels and does not preserve native routing identity. Options C and D both tunnel-encapsulate the traffic, changing outer headers — which breaks the multicast/routing-preservation requirement.

questions.question: Security Operations wants to detect malware in encrypted TLS traffic without decrypting it. Which Cisco capability uses metadata such as initial data packet, sequence of packet lengths and times, and byte distribution to make this judgment?
options: Encrypted Traffic Analytics (ETA) exporting IDP, SPLT, and byte distribution metadata for ML analysis
Umbrella DNS-layer blocking that prevents resolution of known-bad domains before TLS is established across both peers in the failover pair for symmetric behavior
Cisco Secure Workload process-hash matching against a curated allow-list of permitted binaries
Snort 3 with rule suppression to ignore expected encrypted traffic while alerting on anomalies
questions.explanation: ETA exports enhanced NetFlow with IDP (initial data packet), SPLT (sequence of packet lengths and times), and byte distribution. Stealthwatch + Cognitive Analytics + Talos build ML models that detect known malware families without breaking encryption. Option B operates at DNS time and offers no detection inside an established TLS session. Option C inspects process activity on workloads, not encrypted network metadata. Option D is a signature-based IPS that cannot inspect encrypted payloads.

questions.question: An engineer is configuring a Cisco Secure Firewall access control policy. A rule must inspect traffic for intrusions using a balanced Snort ruleset and also log connections. What rule action must be used?
options: Trust, configured with `log at end of connection` to record the bypassed flow
Monitor, which logs the flow before it falls through to the next access control rule
Allow, with an associated intrusion policy and connection logging enabled
Block with reset, paired with file inspection at the policy level
questions.explanation: The Allow action passes traffic through the AC rule while letting attached inspection (intrusion, file, variable set) run on it. Option A bypasses all inspection — Trust is explicitly the no-inspect action. Option B is passive and cannot be terminal; it logs and falls through to other rules. Option D prevents traffic entirely, which is not the goal of inspecting permitted flows.

questions.question: An analyst investigates suspicious PowerShell activity on a Windows endpoint using Cisco Secure Endpoint. They want to isolate the host from the network but keep communication with Secure Endpoint cloud for investigation. Which feature provides this?
options: Host Isolation (Endpoint Isolation) that blocks all traffic except the connector's communication with the cloud
Endpoint IoC retroactive scan, which sweeps the host for indicators after a threat is published with default platform tunables left unchanged for the deployment
Simple Custom Detection list, used to convict files by SHA-256 before they execute
Exclusion set bypass to temporarily ignore selected paths during deep forensic capture
questions.explanation: Secure Endpoint's Host Isolation quarantines an endpoint by blocking all network traffic except the connector's communication back to the cloud, allowing forensics without leaking lateral movement. It can be released remotely once the threat is contained. Option B is a scanning capability, not an isolation mechanism. Option C is a hash-based conviction list, not network isolation. Option D weakens detection and is the opposite of what isolation requires.

questions.question: An organization wants NTP to be authenticated between routers to prevent an attacker from spoofing time and forging log timestamps. Which configuration is correct?
options: `ntp server 10.1.1.1 prefer` without any additional key configuration
`ntp master stratum 5` so each router advertises itself authoritatively to peers for the documented enterprise reference architecture diagrams and consistent with the published vendor reference
`ntp access-group peer 10` referencing an ACL of permitted peer IPs only
Configure `ntp authentication-key`, `ntp authenticate`, and `ntp trusted-key` on both devices, then reference the key on the `ntp server` command
questions.explanation: NTP authentication requires defining a shared key (`ntp authentication-key`), enabling authentication (`ntp authenticate`), marking the key as trusted (`ntp trusted-key`), and binding it on the server statement. Without all four, messages will not be authenticated. Option A only points at a server with no authentication. Option B turns the router into an NTP master and does not provide message authentication. Option C limits which IPs may peer but does not validate the content of NTP messages cryptographically.

questions.question: A security engineer wants an AAA design where the same policy server provides RADIUS for wireless users, 802.1X for wired users, TACACS+ for device admin, and posture checks. Which Cisco product covers all of these in one platform?
options: FreeRADIUS with LDAP for authentication and an external posture engine bolted on for compliance using the recommended Cisco Validated Design template values
Cisco Secure ACS (end-of-life) for combined TACACS+ and RADIUS in legacy environments
Microsoft NPS with Certificate Services for RADIUS and EAP-TLS only on Windows estates
Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE) with the Device Admin license to add TACACS+ alongside RADIUS and posture
questions.explanation: ISE supersedes ACS and supports RADIUS, 802.1X/EAP, posture, profiling, and TACACS+ (via the Device Admin license). A single policy server simplifies policy and reporting. Option A does not natively support TACACS+ or posture in one product. Option B is end-of-life and not a current option. Option C is RADIUS-only and lacks TACACS+ device admin and posture.

questions.question: An engineer configures a Cisco ASA for Active/Standby failover. Which requirement must be met for stateful failover to preserve existing TCP sessions during a failover event?
options: Stateful failover only works when both units are in multi-context routed mode with at least two contexts
Both units must run different software versions so that a single defect does not affect both peers simultaneously consistent with the published platform best-practice guide
A dedicated stateful failover link (or sharing the failover link) connects the two units, and both run identical software and hardware
One unit must run in routed mode and the other in transparent mode so the standby can hot-swap on Layer 2 outage
questions.explanation: Stateful failover replicates the connection table between units over a stateful link (dedicated or shared with the failover link). Both units must have identical hardware, modules, software versions, and licenses. Mixed modes or versions break failover. Option A invents a context-count restriction. Option B contradicts the identical-version requirement and would actually break failover negotiation. Option D mixes incompatible firewall modes.

questions.question: A global enterprise wants to consolidate WAN, SD-WAN, SWG, CASB, ZTNA, and FWaaS into one cloud-delivered offering that follows the user — not the data centre. Branch sites and roaming users connect to the nearest cloud PoP, which enforces a single policy. Which architecture does Gartner call this?
options: Software-Defined Perimeter (SDP), an identity-based dark-cloud access model for individual apps evaluated against the customer's compliance and audit baseline
Secure Access Service Edge (SASE), converging WAN and security as a cloud-delivered service at the nearest PoP
Cisco Catalyst Center (formerly DNA Center), a campus and SD-Access management plane
ACI Multi-Site Orchestrator, a fabric-level orchestration plane for data-centre ACI deployments
questions.explanation: SASE, coined by Gartner, converges WAN (SD-WAN) and network security (SWG, CASB, ZTNA, FWaaS, DNS) as a cloud service. Cisco delivers this via Umbrella SIG, Catalyst SD-WAN, and Duo ZTNA. Option A covers only one component of the stack (per-app ZTNA). Options C and D are campus or data-centre management planes, not a converged cloud edge.

questions.question: A security analyst wants to automate incident response: when Cisco Secure Endpoint detects malware, Umbrella should add the associated domain to a block list, and an investigation ticket should be opened. Which Cisco platform orchestrates multi-product workflows like this?
options: Cisco SecureX Orchestration with workflows composed of atomic actions, HTTP requests, and conditional logic
Cisco Firepower Device Manager (FDM), the on-box manager intended for single-firewall deployments
Cisco Catalyst Center (DNA Center) Assurance, focused on campus network health and telemetry
Cisco Prime Infrastructure, the legacy on-premises network management system for IOS/IOS-XE devices aligned with the SOC operating procedures and runbook entries
questions.explanation: SecureX Orchestration provides drag-and-drop workflows (atomic actions, HTTP requests, logic) that pivot between Secure Endpoint, Umbrella, FMC, Email, Threat Response, ServiceNow, and more. Option B manages a single firewall, not cross-product workflows. Option C is a campus assurance product. Option D is a legacy network management platform; neither performs SOAR.

questions.question: A company evaluates authenticated API access for partners calling its gateway. Which mechanism provides scoped, expiring access tokens and is widely recommended for REST API authentication?
options: Mutual TLS only, with long-lived client certificates and no application-layer authorization scopes documented in the change-management ticket prior to rollout
OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens with scopes and short lifetimes, ideally combined with mTLS for machine-to-machine
HTTP Basic Auth over HTTPS with a shared static password reused across all partners
Static API keys hardcoded into the client application and rotated only on credential incident
questions.explanation: OAuth 2.0 grants scoped, time-bound bearer tokens, supporting rotation and revocation. Static passwords and keys are long-lived secrets that leak easily. Mutual TLS alone cannot express fine-grained scopes; pairing it with OAuth provides strong mutual authentication plus authorization. Option A omits scoped authorization. Options C and D are long-lived shared secrets that are widely discouraged for partner API authentication.

questions.question: A malicious actor is performing a MAC flooding attack against an access switch, causing the CAM table to overflow so that the switch fails open and floods frames. Which mitigation stops this attack?
options: Enable DHCP snooping globally on all VLANs and trust only the uplink to the distribution layer as configured in the standard template provided by the vendor
Increase the CAM table size on the switch via a platform tunable to absorb the attack volume
Enable port-security with a maximum-MAC limit and a restrict or shutdown violation action on access ports
Set `spanning-tree portfast` on access ports to speed up the recovery after a forwarding loop
questions.explanation: Port-security caps the number of distinct source MACs learned on an access port. When exceeded, the port is restricted or shutdown, preventing the CAM overflow that makes a switch flood frames. Option A is for rogue-DHCP defense — a different attack class. Option B is not a supported tunable on Catalyst switches and would not deter the attacker anyway. Option D is a spanning-tree convergence option, unrelated to CAM table protection.

questions.question: A forensic team investigates an insider threat. They need to correlate user login events with network flows and file access from weeks ago. Which Cisco capability stores enriched session context linking username to IP address over time?
options: Catalyst Center user telemetry dashboard, aggregating per-user network experience metrics for campus users
ASA NetFlow Secure Event Logging (NSEL) without pxGrid integration to the identity store
SNMPv3 per-user accounting against the switch CLI for management-plane session tracking
ISE publishing Session Directory via pxGrid so subscribers receive user-to-IP and identity context
questions.explanation: pxGrid is Cisco's Platform Exchange Grid: ISE publishes session context (username, SGT, device type, posture) and subscribers like Stealthwatch, FMC, Secure Endpoint consume it to attribute flows and events to identity, enabling historical user-centric investigation. Option A tracks user experience telemetry, not authentication identity-to-flow correlation. Option B emits flow events but without identity context. Option C accounts for CLI sessions, not endpoint network flows.

questions.question: An engineer must decide between Cisco AnyConnect SSL VPN and IPsec IKEv2 remote access. Remote users are often behind hotel NAT and restrictive firewalls that only allow HTTP/HTTPS. Which option is most likely to succeed in all locations?
options: IKEv2 on UDP 500 with no NAT-T, prioritising the native IPsec ports through the captive network applying the platform-defaults shipped on a fresh installation
IKEv1 main mode on UDP 500 with NAT-T fallback to UDP 4500 when address translation is detected
AnyConnect SSL VPN over TCP 443 (with DTLS on UDP 443 when available) so the tunnel rides standard HTTPS
L2TP over IPsec, relying on Windows built-in client support and a static PSK on the ASA
questions.explanation: SSL VPN over TCP 443 looks like normal HTTPS and traverses almost any NAT or captive portal. DTLS on UDP 443 accelerates once available. IKEv1/IKEv2 over UDP 500/4500 is frequently blocked in guest/hotel networks. Option A explicitly avoids NAT-T, guaranteeing failure behind NAT. Option B still depends on UDP 500/4500 even with fallback. Option D also relies on UDP 500/4500 plus ESP and tends to be the most often blocked.

questions.question: A security architect is briefing leadership on a model that assumes the network is compromised by default, treats every request as untrusted regardless of network origin, and verifies identity + device posture + context on every access decision. The model relies on dynamic policy rather than a static perimeter. Which statement about this architecture is accurate?
options: It assumes the corporate network is trusted by default and applies controls only at the perimeter between internal and external networks across both peers in the failover pair for symmetric behavior
It is a network architecture that assumes no implicit trust based on network location, continuously verifies every access request, and enforces least privilege regardless of network location
It is a synonym for micro-segmentation, referring exclusively to east-west firewalling between workloads in the same data centre
It is a Cisco-specific product family delivered only through ISE and Secure Firewall, not implementable on other vendor stacks
questions.explanation: NIST SP 800-207 defines Zero Trust around three tenets: verify explicitly (identity, device, context), use least-privileged access, and assume breach. Network location is not a trust anchor. Option A is the legacy perimeter model that Zero Trust replaces. Option C narrows Zero Trust to a single technique (micro-seg) that is one component, not the whole architecture. Option D is incorrect — Zero Trust is a vendor-neutral architecture defined by NIST and implementable on any stack.

questions.question: A Snort 3 rule on Cisco Secure Firewall reads: `alert http any any -> any any (msg:"admin path"; http_uri; content:"admin"; sid:1000001;)`. The author is restricting where the content match must appear. Which statement best describes the effect of the `http_uri` modifier in this rule?
options: It restricts the `content` match to the HTTP URI buffer (path plus query) only; the word `admin` elsewhere in headers or body is not matched
It applies the content match to every HTTP header except the URI, the opposite of what the keyword name suggests
It enables URI normalisation but does not constrain where the content match is applied within the HTTP message
It activates rule action `block` whenever the URI contains the string, regardless of where in the URI it appears, and bypasses normalisation as documented in the deployment guide
questions.explanation: Snort 3 introduced buffers (http_uri, http_header, http_client_body, etc.) that isolate where content matching is applied. `http_uri` limits the match to the normalized request URI, preventing false positives from payload elsewhere. Option B inverts the modifier's meaning. Option C confuses the buffer-restriction modifier with a separate normalisation knob. Option D both overrides the rule's `alert` action and falsely claims the modifier disables normalisation.

questions.question: A container security engineer wants to ensure that only signed images from an approved registry can be deployed to a Kubernetes cluster. Which mechanism enforces this at admission time?
options: An Admission Controller policy (for example, OPA Gatekeeper or Kyverno) validating the image registry and cosign signature on every Pod create
Pod Security Admission labels on namespaces, applied without any additional signature verification
A Kubernetes NetworkPolicy denying egress to unknown registries so unsigned images cannot be pulled with default platform tunables left unchanged for the deployment
A ClusterRole limiting which subjects can call `kubectl apply` against the cluster
questions.explanation: Admission controllers validate objects before they are persisted. OPA Gatekeeper or Kyverno policies can require images to come from an approved registry and pass cosign signature verification. Option B handles pod security standards (privileges, capabilities), not image provenance. Option C controls runtime egress, not admission, and image pulls usually happen via the node not the workload. Option D restricts who can submit objects but does nothing to validate the images inside them.

questions.question: A Cisco Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) deployment must block outbound connections to newly registered domains (NRDs) often associated with phishing. Which feature achieves this without maintaining a manual list?
options: Security Intelligence (SI) feeds from Talos, including the newly-registered-domain and DGA categories applied to DNS and URL traffic
A NAT rule with destination zone `any` that redirects outbound traffic into a deny-state pool
Flexible NetFlow sampling tuned to emit logs for outbound DNS, paired with a log-based block
A custom file policy blocking `.zip` and `.iso` files at egress to limit malware download channels for the documented enterprise reference architecture diagrams
questions.explanation: Security Intelligence uses Talos-maintained feeds (malware, phishing, botnets, NRD, DGA) to block, monitor, or allow traffic by IP/URL/DNS reputation before the access control rules fire. It is updated automatically. Option B is not how NAT or SI works — NAT does not enforce reputation. Option C is a flow-export tool, not an enforcement mechanism. Option D blocks file types, which is unrelated to NRD reputation.

questions.question: A cloud team must ensure that EC2 instances cannot reach the Internet but can call AWS services privately. Which configuration meets this?
options: VPC Interface Endpoints (PrivateLink) for required AWS services and no IGW or NAT Gateway route in the route table
Route table with default route to a Transit Gateway that forwards to an on-prem proxy for service calls using the recommended Cisco Validated Design template values
Public subnet with an Elastic IP and stateful NACL allowing only AWS API CIDRs outbound
Security group permitting 0.0.0.0/0 outbound combined with a NAT Gateway for egress
questions.explanation: VPC endpoints (Gateway for S3/DynamoDB, Interface/PrivateLink for most others) route traffic to AWS services over the AWS private backbone without crossing the Internet. Removing the IGW route ensures the subnet is truly private. Option B adds latency and an unnecessary on-prem dependency. Option C still uses public IPs and the public Internet. Option D explicitly grants outbound Internet access, which violates the requirement.

questions.question: An engineer wants to encrypt a flash disk image backup using strong symmetric encryption. Which algorithm offers the best balance of security and performance for 2026-era hardware with AES-NI?
options: AES-256 in GCM mode, providing authenticated encryption accelerated by AES-NI
Blowfish in CBC mode, valued for its small footprint and royalty-free history
DES in ECB mode, attractive for its simplicity and broad legacy support
RC4 with a 128-bit key, marketed for its high throughput on general-purpose CPUs
questions.explanation: AES-256-GCM provides authenticated encryption (confidentiality + integrity) and is hardware-accelerated by AES-NI, making it both fast and secure. Option B is a legacy 64-bit block cipher unsuitable for new designs. Option C is broken: 56-bit keys and ECB mode are both insecure today. Option D is a deprecated stream cipher with documented biases and is removed from modern TLS.

questions.question: An ISE administrator configures a policy where machine authentication must succeed before user authentication is allowed (so only corporate-joined devices can get user access). Which EAP feature provides this?
options: EAP-TLS with an anonymous outer identity to hide the username during the handshake
LEAP with cached credentials so the supplicant remembers prior successful machine logins
PEAP with inner MS-CHAPv2 only, sending both machine and user credentials in the same tunnel consistent with the published platform best-practice guide
EAP chaining with EAP-FAST (or TEAP), authenticating both machine and user in a single exchange
questions.explanation: EAP chaining (originally EAP-FAST, now TEAP in modern deployments) authenticates both machine and user in a single exchange and ties them together so ISE can enforce 'domain-joined device AND valid user' policies. Option A only hides the username; it does not chain identities. Option B is a deprecated lightweight protocol with no chaining concept. Option C runs a single authentication inside one tunnel and cannot tie machine and user identities together.

questions.question: An engineer deploys FlexVPN on a hub-spoke topology using IKEv2. Which feature allows spokes to dynamically build spoke-to-spoke tunnels on demand using shortcut switching?
options: ASA SSL VPN split tunneling, steering corporate subnets into the tunnel and Internet directly
FlexVPN with NHRP shortcut switching, letting the hub redirect spokes to talk directly
IKEv1 aggressive mode with a wildcard PSK across all spokes to speed up tunnel setup
GETVPN with group key distribution from the Key Server to all member sites at once
questions.explanation: FlexVPN supports NHRP redirect/shortcut similar to DMVPN Phase 3, allowing the hub to redirect spokes to each other. Spokes then establish direct on-demand tunnels without hair-pinning through the hub. Option A is a remote-access feature unrelated to spoke-to-spoke tunnels. Option C is a legacy mode with no dynamic spoke-to-spoke behavior and well-known security issues. Option D is a tunnel-less group-key VPN with no concept of dynamic spoke-to-spoke shortcut.

questions.question: A Cisco ESA administrator needs to prevent users from seeing marketing or promotional mail in their inboxes while still letting them opt out. Which ESA capability provides this?
options: Forged Email Detection (FED), which targets CEO-impersonation attempts using a configurable dictionary
Outbreak Filters with a `modify` action that rewrites suspicious URLs in inbound messages
Graymail detection paired with Safe Unsubscribe to filter bulk mail and protect opt-out links
Content Filter with a `quarantine` action for every inbound message containing HTML
questions.explanation: Graymail detection classifies legitimate bulk mail (marketing, social, bulk) and can move it out of the inbox. Safe Unsubscribe lets users opt out via a proxy that protects them from malicious unsubscribe links. Option A targets executive spoofing, not graymail. Option B addresses URL-based threats, not bulk mail classification. Option D quarantines almost all legitimate mail and is not a graymail solution.

questions.question: A corporate policy requires that laptops be automatically enrolled with a client certificate used for 802.1X EAP-TLS when joining the network for the first time. Which ISE workflow accomplishes this?
options: BYOD onboarding flow with the ISE provisioning portal issuing certificates via internal CA or SCEP/NDES
Posture portal with the AnyConnect compliance module evaluating registry keys on the endpoint evaluated against the customer's compliance and audit baseline
Device Administration portal with TACACS+ authorization for command-level audit
Guest portal with a voucher code emailed by the sponsoring employee at the time of arrival
questions.explanation: The BYOD/Onboarding flow uses a provisioning portal that installs a certificate profile. ISE can act as its own internal CA or forward requests via SCEP to Microsoft NDES/ADCS. The device then uses EAP-TLS with that cert for ongoing authentication. Option B is a compliance flow, not a certificate enrollment flow. Option C handles network device admin AAA. Option D is a visitor self-registration flow that does not provision certificates.

questions.question: A security engineer wants to prevent IP address spoofing at the edge of the network so that attackers cannot forge source addresses from inside routed segments. Which IOS feature accomplishes this at the interface level?
options: Unicast Reverse Path Forwarding (uRPF) in strict mode applied on the customer-facing interfaces
Port-security with maximum 1 MAC per port to limit how many endpoints share a connection
Control Plane Policing (CoPP) policing inbound traffic destined to the router itself
`no ip directed-broadcast` to prevent the legacy directed-broadcast amplification behavior aligned with the SOC operating procedures and runbook entries
questions.explanation: Strict-mode uRPF accepts a packet only if the source address is reachable via the interface it came in on (symmetric path). This blocks spoofed packets at the edge (BCP 38). Option B is a Layer 2 feature limiting MAC learning; it does not validate source IP. Option C protects the route processor from floods, not data-plane source spoofing. Option D mitigates broadcast amplification but does not stop unicast source IP spoofing.

questions.question: An engineer designs Secure Internet access for branch offices. Umbrella SIG policy must apply per user identity. Which integration makes Umbrella cloud firewall and SWG aware of user identities from Active Directory?
options: Umbrella Roaming Client only, relying on local Windows identity at the endpoint without an AD connector
SNMP polling of the domain controller from Umbrella to extract logged-on user information
Umbrella Virtual Appliance only, deployed at each site for DNS forwarding without identity sync
Umbrella Active Directory Connector syncing user-to-IP mappings from domain controllers to Umbrella
questions.explanation: Umbrella AD Connector pushes user-to-IP mappings from domain controllers so that Umbrella policies in-network can be user-scoped; for roaming users, the AnyConnect Umbrella/SWG module signs requests with identity. Option A alone identifies the roaming user but does not deliver AD identity for in-branch traffic. Option B is not a supported integration method. Option C provides only resolver-level visibility per source IP, not per AD user.

questions.question: A forensic engineer must validate the integrity of a captured disk image against its original. Which cryptographic function is most appropriate to produce a collision-resistant fingerprint in 2026?
options: MD5, valued historically for fast computation and broad tooling availability
SHA-1, still accepted in some legacy forensic procedures and tool chains
SHA-256 (SHA-2 family) or SHA-3, the current standards for collision-resistant hashing
CRC32, efficient and standardised for transmission and storage integrity checks documented in the change-management ticket prior to rollout
questions.explanation: MD5 and SHA-1 have practical collision attacks and are no longer considered collision-resistant. CRC32 is an error-detection code, not a cryptographic hash. SHA-256 (SHA-2) or SHA-3 are the current standards for forensic integrity hashing. Option A is broken for collision resistance. Option B is also broken (SHAttered, 2017) and is being phased out of compliance-grade forensic workflows. Option D detects accidental flips but offers no cryptographic resistance to manipulation.
